title: NumPy fundamentals
summary: Create and manipulate NumPy arrays, and explain why NumPy is faster than plain Python lists for numeric work.
objectives: Turn a Python list into a NumPy array with np.array()
Use array methods such as .mean(), .max(), .min() and .std()
Apply one operation to every element at once (vectorised arithmetic)
Explain why NumPy code avoids loops for numeric work

segments.title: What you will build
segments.body:
## What you will build

A Python list can hold exam scores, but working out statistics with loops is slow to write and slow to run. NumPy stores numbers in an array and does the arithmetic on all of them at once, which is why data science code uses it everywhere. In this lab you will turn a list of eight exam scores into a NumPy array and compute the mean, the highest and lowest score and the standard deviation with array methods. You will then add a 5-mark curve to every score in one line, with no loop at all, and print the results.

lab.title: Exam scores with NumPy
lab.objective: Turn a list of scores into a NumPy array and compute statistics and a +5 curve with vectorised operations.
lab.instructions:
The list scores_list holds eight exam scores. Using NumPy (import numpy as np):

1. Make scores = np.array(scores_list).
2. Compute mean_score = scores.mean(), highest = scores.max(), lowest = scores.min() and spread = scores.std().
3. Make curved = scores + 5 (every score plus five, in one line, with no loop).
4. Print five lines:
Mean: 77.75
Highest: 95
Lowest: 58
Standard deviation: 11.85
Curved: [77, 90, 95, 69, 63, 100, 82, 86]

Round the standard deviation only when printing, with round(spread, 2), and print curved with curved.tolist().
lab.constraints: Use NumPy array methods and array arithmetic; no for or while loops. Keep the names scores_list, scores, mean_score, highest, lowest, spread and curved. No input().
lab.starter_code:
import numpy as np

scores_list = [72, 85, 90, 64, 58, 95, 77, 81]

# 1. Turn the list into a NumPy array called scores


# 2. Compute mean_score, highest, lowest and spread (standard deviation)
#    using the array's own methods


# 3. Make curved: every score plus 5, in ONE line, without a loop


# 4. Print the five lines shown in the instructions
hints: np.array(scores_list) gives you an array. Arrays have their own methods: scores.mean(), scores.max(), scores.min() and scores.std().
Arithmetic on an array applies to every element: scores + 5 is a new array where every score is 5 higher. Store it in curved.
Print with labels, for example print("Mean:", mean_score) and print("Standard deviation:", round(spread, 2)). For the last line use print("Curved:", curved.tolist()).

visible_examples.code:
import numpy as np

marks = np.array([10, 20, 30])
print("Mean:", marks.mean())
print("Highest:", marks.max())

visible_examples.description: One operation on every element at once
visible_examples.code:
import numpy as np

prices = np.array([5, 8, 11])
doubled = prices * 2
print(doubled.tolist())

success_criteria: scores is a NumPy array made from scores_list
Your output includes the line: Mean: 77.75
mean_score, highest and lowest hold the right statistics
spread holds the standard deviation of the scores
curved is a NumPy array made with one vectorised operation, not a loop

tests.label: scores is a NumPy array
tests.objective: Create a NumPy array from a list

tests.label: The mean is printed
tests.remediation: Compute mean_score = scores.mean() and print it as print("Mean:", mean_score).

tests.label: curved is every score plus 5
tests.remediation: Make curved = scores + 5. NumPy adds 5 to every element for you.

tests.label: mean_score, highest and lowest are right
tests.remediation: Use the array methods: mean_score = scores.mean(), highest = scores.max(), lowest = scores.min().

tests.label: spread is the standard deviation
tests.remediation: spread = scores.std() gives the standard deviation of the array. Do not round the variable itself; round only when printing.

tests.label: curved is a NumPy array of 8 values
tests.remediation: curved must be a NumPy array made with array arithmetic (scores + 5), not a list built with a loop.

lab.solution:
import numpy as np

scores_list = [72, 85, 90, 64, 58, 95, 77, 81]

scores = np.array(scores_list)

mean_score = scores.mean()
highest = scores.max()
lowest = scores.min()
spread = scores.std()

curved = scores + 5

print("Mean:", mean_score)
print("Highest:", highest)
print("Lowest:", lowest)
print("Standard deviation:", round(spread, 2))
print("Curved:", curved.tolist())
